sources.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
sources.locator: Complete full-text PDF/text inspected for §§2.1–2.4 (PDF pp. 22–30): nilpotent Jordan-quiver category, Hall-number examples, polynomial Hall algebra, symmetric-function isomorphism, and the Green power-sum pairing.

contents.name: Theorem 2.1: Jordan-quiver nilpotent representations and partition classification
contents.reason: The partition classification is already locally owned by batch 50 through lem-jordan-quiver-isoclasses-are-partition-indexed; batch 53 uses that supplier without duplicating it.

contents.name: Examples 2.2–2.4: Jordan-quiver Hall-number and flag counts
contents.reason: The Jordan square and related Hall-count computations are already owned by the batch-50 examples page; this pair uses those exact conventions rather than repeating them.

contents.name: Theorem 2.6 and Proposition 2.7: the classical Hall algebra and Hall-polynomial construction
contents.reason: The generic Jordan Hall algebra and its full local Hall-polynomial proof are assigned to batch 50; the current page consumes the actual bodies and adds module/Fock structure.

contents.name: Lemma 2.8: automorphism count for a Jordan-quiver representation
contents.reason: The automorphism formula is already a local batch-50 supplier used by its Jordan pairing theorem; this pair does not duplicate the count.

contents.name: Theorem 2.9 and equation (2.9): Hall algebra to symmetric functions and Green power-sum norms
contents.reason: The source fixes the generator map and Green norm; the new Fock proof uses the actual batch-50 isomorphism and pairing supplier, then derives the normalized adjoint and commutators locally.

contents.name: Remark 2.10: geometric lift of the Hall-to-symmetric-function map
contents.reason: The flag-variety and spherical-Hecke geometric lift is beyond the present algebraic regular-module and normalized-Fock argument; no geometric lift is claimed here.

sources.title: I. G. Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed.
sources.locator: Chapter I §4, equation (4.5), equations (4.6)–(4.7), and Remark 8 (printed pp. 63–68): dual Hall bases, Cauchy kernel, power-sum norms and the symmetric-algebra extension of the form.

contents.name: Equation (4.5): the Hall form dualizes complete and monomial symmetric-function bases
contents.reason: The local definition of the ordinary Hall form is already published and is used only for the normalization comparison.

contents.name: Equations (4.6)–(4.7): the Cauchy kernel gives the power-sum norm z_lambda
contents.reason: The power-sum orthogonality and norm formula are already published; the companion example cites this exact supplier.

contents.name: Remark 8: extension of the Hall form from the power-sum basis
contents.reason: The local degree-r comparison computes the Green adjoint against the ordinary Hall adjoint and makes the q-parameter rescaling explicit.

sources.title: Hiraku Nakajima, Introduction to quiver varieties—for ring and representation theorists, arXiv:1611.10000v1
sources.locator: Complete 19-page note inspected for context; read §§2.2, 3.2 Definition 6 and Example 10, and §§4.2–4.5, including the A1 stability example, Hecke correspondence, convolution convention, no-edge-loop condition and general-action proof sketch.

contents.name: Section 2.2: framed representations and the moment-map equation
contents.reason: The A1 item defines I:W→V, J:V→W, the equation IJ=0 and the precise GL(V) action.

contents.name: Section 3.2 Definition 6 and Example 10: positive stability for A1
contents.reason: For the one-vertex quiver with positive stability, the source identifies stability with injectivity of J and the A1 moduli space with T*Gr(v,W); the local proof specializes this directly to v=0,1.

contents.name: Section 4.2: A1 weight spaces of the fundamental sl2 representation
contents.reason: The source supplies the weight convention; the local proof derives the two point classes and verifies every bracket on them.

contents.name: Section 4.3: Borel–Moore correspondence convolution and the diagonal identity
contents.reason: The source fixes the fundamental-class correspondence convention; for the point spaces the local definition reduces it to the unique point-class map.

contents.name: Section 4.4: framed Hecke correspondence as a short exact sequence
contents.reason: The A1 definition spells out the subdatum and quotient S and the local proof verifies the incidence point without importing a general action theorem.

contents.name: Section 4.5 Theorem 17 and its proof sketch: loopless-quiver Kac–Moody action
contents.reason: The note states the general no-edge-loop theorem but sketches rather than supplies its complete relation proof; this pair proves only the exact A1 correspondence instance and makes no general Kac–Moody claim.
